caption:
Scripture is meant to be read aloud.
Esoteric scripture is meant to be withheld.

The Zohar wore the name of a second-century sage.
Scholarship places it in thirteenth-century Castile.

Renaissance readers believed Hermes Trismegistus as old as Moses.
Casaubon redated his Corpus in 1614.

A jar in Upper Egypt held the Gospel of Thomas for sixteen centuries.
A Tibetan treasure text guides the dead through the bardo.
A Swedish scientist claimed to report what he saw among the spirits.

False antiquity was not always deception.
It was a way of saying: this did not come from a man.
It came through one.

Which of these would you open first? Answer below.

The full entry waits in the Forbidden Library: alloccult.com/grimoires-sacred-texts/religious-esoteric-texts

review_log.summary: A strong, accurate carousel with good images. It needs a few text fixes before posting. Slide 3 calls the Gospel of Thomas's promise a 'warning' and lacks the place-and-date kicker the other slides use. Slide 2's opening is clumsy. Slide 4 overclaims Hermes as 'older than' Moses, which the caption itself softens to 'the age of Moses'. Slide 6's kicker breaks the place-and-date format. Slide 7's question names Sefer Yetzirah, which the carousel never covers, and leaves out the Corpus Hermeticum. The hashtags should follow that change. The caption is good.
fixes: slide 2 text: 'The Zohar claimed a second-century sage' is clumsy: a book does not claim a sage. The authorship claim should be stated plainly.
slide 3 text: Saying 1 ('will not taste death') is a promise, not a warning, so the text mischaracterises it. The kicker also lacks the place-and-date format used on the other slides.
slide 4 text: 'Older than Moses' overclaims. Renaissance readers such as Ficino generally made Hermes a contemporary of Moses. The caption already says 'the age of Moses', so the slide should match.
slide 6 text: The kicker 'Swedenborg · 1749' breaks the place-and-date format of the other slides. Arcana Coelestia's first volume was published in London in 1749.
slide 7 text: The question lists Sefer Yetzirah, which appears on no slide, and omits the Corpus Hermeticum, which does. The choices should match the books shown.

review_log.summary: Strong, accurate carousel with fitting public-domain images. Three text fixes are needed. Slide 3 never names the Gospel of Thomas, which slide 7 relies on. Slide 4 has a clumsy construction ('believed as old as'). Slide 6 never names Swedenborg and implies his visions began in 1749, when they began in the mid-1740s. Images, cover legibility, end card and caption all pass.
fixes: slide 3 text: The slide quotes the incipit but never names the Gospel of Thomas. Slide 7 asks the reader to choose 'Thomas', so the text must be identified here.
slide 4 text: 'Was believed as old as Moses' is clumsy. 'The spell broke' slightly overclaims, since Hermetic devotion outlived Casaubon.

slide 6 text: Swedenborg is never named in the text. 'Began reporting the spirit world' paired with 1749 misdates the start of his visions, which began c. 1744–45. 1749 is when the first volume of Arcana Coelestia was published.

review_log.summary: Strong, accurate carousel with fitting public-domain images. Two fixes are needed before posting. Slide 2 overclaims twice: the Zohar does not itself name an author, and Moses de León was suspected long before Scholem, so 'named another' is wrong. The caption says the Corpus Hermeticum 'claimed the age of Moses', but that antiquity was assigned by Renaissance readers, not claimed by the texts. All other slides are accurate and legible.
fixes: slide 2 text: Overclaims on two points. The Zohar does not 'name its author'; it speaks through Shimon bar Yochai as its master teacher. Moses de León was suspected as early as the 14th century, so Scholem did not first 'name' him; his 1941 Major Trends made the decisive case.

caption: 'The Corpus Hermeticum claimed the age of Moses' is inaccurate. The texts do not claim this; Renaissance readers such as Ficino placed Hermes near the time of Moses. Swedenborg also appears in the carousel but not in the caption, so a line is added for consistency.

review_log.summary: Strong, accurate carousel with a good hook, but two slides need fixing before posting. Slide 2 says Scholem 'proved' de León's authorship, which overclaims: the archive says he made a 'decisive demonstration', and later scholarship suggests a circle of authors. Slide 6's image is a cluttered Victorian advertisement for William White's biography rather than a clean portrait, and its wording is clumsy. All other slides, the end card and the caption pass.
fixes: slide 2 text: 'Proved its true author' overclaims. The archive calls it Scholem's 'decisive demonstration' that 'attributes' the Zohar to de León, and later scholars argue for a circle of authors.

slide 6 image: The image is a Victorian publisher's advertisement for William White's biography, crowded with press reviews and prices. It reads as a book ad, not a portrait, and clashes with the brand's tone.
slide 6 text: 'Claimed to report the spirit world' is clumsy, and the sentence needs 'His' before Arcana Coelestia.

review_log.summary: Clean final pass, approved. All facts are accurate and match the archive: Zohar and Moses de León (Scholem, 1941), Casaubon in London in 1614, Nag Hammadi in 1945, Karma Lingpa in the 14th century, and the first Arcana Coelestia volume in London in 1749. Images fit their subjects. The cover hook reads clearly over the diagram. Only minor polish remains: the Kabbalah Unveiled plates appear on three slides, but each is a different plate and on-topic.
